title: SARS-CoV-2 and neutralizing antibody dynamics at a remote village in Kenya before widespread COVID-19 vaccine rollout
abstract: Given limited data on SARS‐CoV‐2 transmission and immunity in rural, low‐vaccine‐coverage settings, we evaluated infection rates and population‐level neutralizing antibody increase in a rural community in western Kenya. The study was conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System that has a population of 160,000. Clusters of households that had representative demographics were identified and individuals invited to participate in six cross-sectional surveys that targeted 234 participants at each survey, two months apart, conducted between April 2021 and March 2022, during which time, the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves dominated. At each survey, participants provided naso-pharyngeal samples for SARS-CoV-2 detection and serum for measuring neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) using surrogate virus neutralizing test which assessed inhibition of RBD–ACE2 binding. 69% (917/1329) of the participants were females. By RT-qPCR, SARS-CoV-2 increased from 3% (7/224) at survey one (April 2021) to 24% (55/229) by survey two (June 2021), and thereafter decreased to zero, only to rise to 10% (23/234) during the January 2022 Omicron wave. NAbs increased from 18% (40/224) at survey one to 86% (202/234) by end of the study. The quantity of NAbs rose from geometric mean of 0.42 U/mL at survey one to 9.4 U/mL by survey six. Females had higher NAbs (3.73U/mL, 95% CI), compared to 1.98 U/mL, 95% CI (p = 0.0146) for males. NAbs quantities increased with age: 2.1 U/mL for 60 years. The increase in population-level NAbs is consistent with widespread exposure to the virus during the study period. As caveat, causality of NAbs for the decline in SARS‐CoV‐2 infections cannot be inferred with confidence, because other factors such as the use of non‐pharmaceutical interventions and other individual-level variables were not measured.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focused on SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and neutralizing antibody dynamics in a rural Kenyan population with limited vaccine coverage, specifically evaluating infection prevalence and population-level neutralizing antibody increases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This was a longitudinal study conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System with 160,000 people. Six cross-sectional surveys targeted 234 participants each, two months apart, between April 2021 and March 2022, during Alpha, Delta, and Omicron waves. Naso-pharyngeal samples and serum were collected for SARS-CoV-2 detection and neutralizing antibody measurement using surrogate virus neutralizing tests.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: SARS-CoV-2 infection rates increased from 3% to 24% then decreased to zero before rising to 10% during Omicron. Neutralizing antibodies increased from 18% to 86% overall, with geometric mean rising from 0.42 U/mL to 9.4 U/mL. Females had higher NAbs than males, and NAbs quantities increased with age.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study could not confidently infer causality between neutralizing antibodies and reduced SARS-CoV-2 infections due to unmeasured factors like non-pharmaceutical interventions and individual-level variables.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the importance of studying SARS-CoV-2 transmission and immunity in rural, low-vaccine-coverage settings to understand infection dynamics and immune responses in such populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and neutralizing antibody dynamics in a rural Kenyan population with limited vaccine coverage. Six cross-sectional surveys conducted between April 2021 and March 2022 showed infection rates fluctuating from 3% to 24% and peaking at 10% during Omicron, while neutralizing antibodies increased from 18% to 86% overall. Females had higher antibody levels than males, and antibody quantities increased with age. The study could not establish causality between antibodies and reduced infections due to unmeasured confounding factors. These findings provide valuable insights into SARS-CoV-2 transmission and immunity in rural, low-vaccine-coverage settings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注 疫苗 覆盖范围有限的肯尼亚农村人口中的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染率和中和抗体动态,特别评估感染 患病率 和人群水平中和抗体的增加。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项在 KEMRI/WRAIR-非洲健康人口统计 监测 系统中进行的纵向研究,涉及 160,000 人。2021 年 4 月至 2022 年 3 月期间,在 Alpha、Delta 和 Omicron 浪潮期间,开展了六项横断面调查,每次针对 234 名参与者,间隔两个月。收集鼻咽样本和血清用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 检测和使用替代病毒中和测试的中和抗体测量。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在 Omicron 期间,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染率从 3% 增加到 24%,然后下降到零,最后上升到 10%。中和抗体总体从 18% 增加到 86%,几何平均值从 0.42 U/mL 增加到 9.4 U/mL。女性的 Nab 含量高于男性,并且 Nab 的数量随着年龄的增长而增加。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于非药物干预措施和个体水平变量等未测量因素,该研究无法自信地推断中和抗体与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染减少之间的因果关系。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了在农村、低 疫苗 覆盖率环境中研究 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 传播 和免疫力的重要性,以了解此类人群中的感染动态和 免疫应答。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The study focused on SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and neutralizing antibody dynamics in a rural Kenyan population with limited vaccine coverage, specifically evaluating infection prevalence and population-level neutralizing antibody increases.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This was a longitudinal study conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System with 160,000 people. Six cross-sectional surveys targeted 234 participants each, two months apart, between April 2021 and March 2022, during Alpha, Delta, and Omicron waves. Naso-pharyngeal samples and serum were collected for SARS-CoV-2 detection and neutralizing antibody measurement using surrogate virus neutralizing tests.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: SARS-CoV-2 infection rates increased from 3% to 24% then decreased to zero before rising to 10% during Omicron. analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study could not confidently infer causality between neutralizing antibodies and reduced SARS-CoV-2 infections due to unmeasured factors like non-pharmaceutical interventions and individual-level variables.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the importance of studying SARS-CoV-2 transmission and immunity in rural, low-vaccine-coverage settings to understand infection dynamics and immune responses in such populations.

title_zh: SARS-CoV-2 and neutralizing antibody dynamics at a remote village in Kenya before widespread COVID-19 vaccine rollout
source_body_en: Given limited data on SARS‐CoV‐2 transmission and immunity in rural, low‐vaccine‐coverage settings, we evaluated infection rates and population‐level neutralizing antibody increase in a rural community in western Kenya. The study was conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System that has a population of 160,000. Clusters of households that had representative demographics were identified and individuals invited to participate in six cross-sectional surveys that targeted 234 participants at each survey, two months apart, conducted between April 2021 and March 2022, during which time, the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves dominated. At each survey, participants provided naso-pharyngeal samples for SARS-CoV-2 detection and serum for measuring neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) using surrogate virus neutralizing test which assessed inhibition of RBD–ACE2 binding. 69% (917/1329) of the participants were females. By RT-qPCR, SARS-CoV-2 increased from 3% (7/224) at survey one (April 2021) to 24% (55/229) by survey two (June 2021), and thereafter decreased to zero, only to rise to 10% (23/234) during the January 2022 Omicron wave. NAbs increased from 18% (40/224) at survey one to 86% (202/234) by end of the study. The quantity of NAbs rose from geometric mean of 0.42 U/mL at survey one to 9.4 U/mL by survey six. Females had higher NAbs (3.73U/mL, 95% CI), compared to 1.98 U/mL, 95% CI (p = 0.0146) for males. NAbs quantities increased with age: 2.1 U/mL for 60 years. The increase in population-level NAbs is consistent with widespread exposure to the virus during the study period. As caveat, causality of NAbs for the decline in SARS‐CoV‐2 infections cannot be inferred with confidence, because other factors such as the use of non‐pharmaceutical interventions and other individual-level variables were not measured.

title: Ensitrelvir for the Treatment of Hospitalized Adults With COVID-19: An International Phase 3 Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Antivirals remain an important treatment strategy for persons who experience severe and life-threatening COVID-19. Ensitrelvir is an oral 3CL protease inhibitor with potent antiviral activity. METHODS: We conducted an international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of ensitrelvir with standard of care (SOC) among adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The primary outcome was clinical recovery assessed by the days to recovery scale through day 60 (DRS-60), analyzed using a Van Elteren test. RESULTS: From 2023 to 2025, 589 participants received blinded study treatment (293 ensitrelvir and 296 placebo). Median age was 69 years, 49% were female, 68% were White, and SOC commonly included corticosteroids (61% and 54%) and remdesivir (62% and 60%) in ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively. Median DRS-60 category was 6 (IQR: 3-15) in the ensitrelvir and 5.5 (IQR: 3-12) in the placebo group (P = .19), and the OR was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.62-1.09) for a better DRS-60 category with ensitrelvir. Ensitrelvir participants had lower detectable viral antigen in plasma at Day 5 (13.4% vs 25.1%; P < .001). There was no difference in secondary clinical outcomes or prespecified safety outcomes, though the mortality rate was 6.1% vs 4.4% and the frequency of hemorrhagic events was 3.4% vs 0.3% among ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Ensitrelvir treatment did not improve clinical recovery in addition to SOC for adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The lower illness severity in the Omicron era compared with earlier periods in the COVID-19 pandemic and high use of remdesivir and corticosteroids, may have contributed to the lack of clinical benefit.

analysis.summary_en: This international phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluated ensitrelvir, an oral 3CL protease inhibitor, for treating hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The study included 589 participants (293 ensitrelvir, 296 placebo) with a median age of 69 years, and standard care commonly included corticosteroids and remdesivir. The primary outcome, clinical recovery measured by DRS-60, showed no significant difference between groups (median 6 vs 5.5, P = .19; OR 0.82). title: Mucosal boosting of chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine encoding SARS-CoV-2 RBD-heterodimer provides robust protection in mice
abstract: ABSTRACT The major route of COVID-19 vaccination currently is via intramuscular injection. Data from clinical trials and real-world studies have demonstrated its effectiveness in preventing severe illness and death caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, its protective efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission in situ remains relatively low. Given that SARS-CoV-2, especially the Omicron variant and its sub-variants, primarily infects and replicates in the human upper respiratory tract, mucosal immune responses are crucial for preventing viral infection. Therefore, we constructed a chimpanzee adenovirus (AdC68)-vectored vaccine expressing the Delta-XBB receptor-binding domain (RBD)-dimer and comprehensively compared the immune responses induced by intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation. Our results revealed that aerosol inhalation of the recombinant AdC68 vaccine induced robust systemic and mucosal immune responses and immune memory, particularly activating memory T cells in the lungs with a long duration in the mouse model. Additionally, we assessed long-term protection against a SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge after ~6 months following a booster vaccination with AdC68-Delta-XBB via different immunization routes. We found that, compared with the intramuscular route, aerosol inhalation provided significantly better protection, without detectable replicating virus in the nasal tissue. This study demonstrates that the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induces robust mucosal immune responses via aerosol inhalation vaccination and prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection in mucosa. IMPORTANCE Immunity induced by first-generation COVID-19 vaccines administered by intramuscular injection is highly effective against severe disease and death but is limited in its ability to prevent viral infection and transmission. A more cost-effective and practical vaccine delivered by the respiratory route is needed to better understand mucosal immune responses and to assess protective efficacy. This study evaluated the immune responses and protective efficacy elicited by intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation of AdC68-Delta-XBB in a mouse model and demonstrated that the aerosol inhalation approach is particularly advantageous for robustly stimulating both systemic and mucosal immune responses. These findings will help guide future clinical development and provide a basis for developing vaccines against other respiratory pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed because current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines, while effective against severe disease, have limited ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission, particularly in the upper respiratory tract where the virus primarily replicates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared immune responses and protective efficacy of an AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine delivered via intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation in a mouse model, with long-term protection assessed against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge approximately 6 months post-booster.
analysis.methods: Researchers constructed a chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine expressing the Delta-XBB receptor-binding domain dimer and evaluated immune responses and protection in mice after different immunization routes, including assessment of memory T cells in the lungs and viral replication in nasal tissue.
analysis.main_results: Aerosol inhalation of the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induced robust systemic and mucosal immune responses and immune memory, particularly activating memory T cells in the lungs with long duration, and provided significantly better protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge compared to intramuscular injection, with no detectable replicating virus in nasal tissue.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that aerosol inhalation vaccination is particularly advantageous for robustly stimulating both systemic and mucosal immune responses, and this study demonstrates that the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induces robust mucosal immune responses via aerosol inhalation to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection in mucosa.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings will guide future clinical development of mucosal vaccines against COVID-19 and provide a basis for developing vaccines against other respiratory pathogens, potentially offering more effective protection against infection and transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted in a mouse model, which may not fully translate to human immune responses and protection; however, the comprehensive comparison of immunization routes and assessment of both immune responses and long-term protection provide substantial support for the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study addressed the limitation of current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission, particularly in the upper respiratory tract. Researchers compared an AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine delivered via intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation in mice. The aerosol inhalation route induced robust systemic and mucosal immune responses, activated lung memory T cells long-term, and provided significantly better protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge with no detectable viral replication in nasal tissue. These findings demonstrate the potential of mucosal vaccination to prevent infection and transmission, guiding future clinical development of more effective COVID-19 vaccines and vaccines against other respiratory pathogens.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了 免疫应答 和 AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 在小鼠模型中通过肌内注射、鼻内给药或气雾吸入给药的保护功效,并在加强剂后约 6 个月评估了针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1 攻击的长期保护作用。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员构建了表达 Delta-XBB 受体结合域二聚体的黑猩猩腺病毒载体 疫苗,并评估了 免疫应答 和不同免疫途径后对小鼠的保护作用,包括评估肺部记忆 T 细胞和鼻组织中的病毒复制。
analysis_zh.main_results: AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 的气雾吸入诱导了强大的全身和粘膜 免疫应答 和免疫记忆,特别是长时间激活肺部的记忆 T 细胞,与肌内注射相比,对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1 攻击提供了明显更好的保护,鼻组织中没有检测到复制病毒。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,气雾吸入 疫苗接种 对于强烈刺激全身和粘膜 免疫应答 特别有利,这项研究表明,AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 通过气雾吸入诱导强劲的粘膜 免疫应答,以防止粘膜中的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,这可能无法完全转化为人类 免疫应答 和保护;然而,免疫途径的综合比较以及免疫应答和长期保护的评估为结论提供了实质性支持。

title: Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccinations for Immunocompromised Children and Household Contacts.
abstract: Immunocompromised pediatric patients, including hematopoietic cell and solid organ transplant recipients, those undergoing chemotherapy for malignancy, and those receiving biologic response modifiers for autoimmune or inflammatory conditions, are at risk for severe disease from vaccine-preventable respiratory viral infections such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). These children face higher rates of hospitalization, intensive care admissions, and mortality, reflecting contributions from an immature immune system, absence of immunologic memory, and/or increased environmental exposures. Immunization recommendations for immunocompromised children are largely extrapolated from studies conducted among healthy children and/or immunocompromised adults due to a paucity of primary data on immunological responses and vaccine efficacy in immunocompromised children. Trends in vaccine hesitancy in the general population, ongoing transmission of respiratory viral infections in the community, and suboptimal vaccination rates among immunocompromised children and their household contacts further compound the risk for this vulnerable population. As the number of children with immunocompromising conditions expands, it is imperative that primary care practitioners and subspecialists who care for immunocompromised children ensure appropriate immunizations are provided to these patients and their household and community contacts. We will review available data supporting the current guidelines regarding vaccine dosing, scheduling, and formulations to prevent influenza, COVID-19, and RSV infections in immunocompromised children. Furthermore, we highlight key knowledge gaps and areas of current investigation aimed at improving respiratory viral vaccine immunogenicity and optimize protection.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the increased risk of severe disease from influenza, COVID-19, and RSV in immunocompromised children, including transplant recipients, chemotherapy patients, and those on biologic therapies. These children face higher hospitalization and mortality rates due to immune system vulnerabilities. Current vaccination recommendations are largely extrapolated from healthy children and adult data, as specific pediatric immunocompromised studies are lacking. The review highlights compounded risks from vaccine hesitancy, community transmission, and suboptimal vaccination rates. Key knowledge gaps exist in vaccine immunogenicity and protection optimization. The authors emphasize the need for practitioners to ensure appropriate vaccinations for these children and their contacts, with future research focused on improving outcomes in this vulnerable population.

title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
abstract: Background: Physiotherapists played central roles in high-risk 'red-zone' care during COVID-19 and reported substantial distress, yet mechanisms linking exposure to burnout remain unclear. Objective: To examine whether the association between direct patient contact and burnout operates through a stress-related behavioural mediator (feeling like quitting/taking a break) and whether organisational resources moderate this pathway. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of a nationwide, multicentre, web-based survey of Japanese physiotherapists engaged in COVID-19 care (March 2021). Burnout was defined using the Japanese MBI-GS case algorithm. Counterfactual mediation analysis with bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstraps (5,000 resamples) was used to estimate the average causal mediation effect (ACME), average direct effect (ADE), and total effect on the risk-difference scale. Models were adjusted for age, sex, years in practice, and cohabitation. Results: Burnout prevalence was 19.4%. A small indirect effect was observed (ACME = 0.00932; 95% CI 0.00188-0.0200), whereas the direct and total effects were not statistically significant. Appreciation/respect was associated with attenuation of the indirect effect (ACME = 0.00007), whereas endorsement of enhanced reimbursement for two-therapist care of critically ill patients was associated with a larger indirect effect (ACME = 0.00637; 95% CI 0.00122-0.0100). Because the primary mediation analysis used a binary mediator and binary outcome with logistic link functions, a formal ρ-based sensitivity analysis for unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding was not available under this specification. Conclusions: Among Japanese physiotherapists, the association between direct COVID-19 patient contact and burnout was consistent with an indirect pathway operating through a stress-related behavioural mediator. Recognition appeared to buffer this pathway, whereas reimbursement-linked resource strain appeared to amplify it. These findings suggest potentially relevant organisational targets for future intervention, but should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and the causal assumptions required for mediation analysis.

title: COVID-19 Vaccination Refusal and Non-Uptake Among People Living with HIV in the United States.
abstract: More than a million individuals in the United States are living with HIV and constitute a particularly vulnerable group for morbidity and mortality associated with COVID-19. Despite the early availability and prioritization of this group for COVID-19 vaccination, notable levels of vaccine refusal and non-uptake have been reported among this group. This scoping review aimed to investigate the nature and extent of COVID-19 vaccine refusal and non-uptake among people living with HIV (PLWH) in the USA. A comprehensive literature search was performed utilizing multiple scholarly databases for studies published between December 2020 and May 2026 that reported on COVID-19 vaccine refusal or non-uptake rates among PLWH in the USA. Data extraction focused on sample size, refusal/non-uptake rates, reasons for refusal, and vaccination enablers. A total of 27 studies were included, encompassing 185,430 PLWH from various settings across the U.S. and the COVID-19 vaccination refusal and non-uptake rates varied from 3.8% to 57.9% [average across all studies=21.0% (95% CI=16.2-26.2%)]. Major barriers identified included medical mistrust, apprehensions regarding vaccine safety and side effects, misinformation, structural issues such as poverty and housing instability, and sociodemographic factors (e.g., sexual/ethnic minority status, lower income or education). Conversely, enablers of vaccination included older age, male gender, White race, active engagement in HIV care, previous vaccination history, recommendations from trusted providers, and higher perceived infection risk or belief in vaccination. The refusal and non-uptake rates for COVID-19 vaccines among PLWH in the USA are considerable and influenced by multiple factors. Interventions should focus on addressing systemic mistrust and psychosocial or structural obstacles while utilizing the existing HIV care framework to increase vaccination rates in this population.

Data extraction focused on sample size, refusal/non-uptake rates, reasons for refusal, and vaccination enablers. A total of 27 studies were included, encompassing 185,430 PLWH from various settings across the U.S. and the COVID-19 vaccination refusal and non-uptake rates varied from 3.8% to 57.9% [average across all studies=21.0% (95% CI=16.2-26.2%)]. Major barriers identified included medical mistrust, apprehensions regarding vaccine safety and side effects, misinformation, structural issues such as poverty and housing instability, and sociodemographic factors (e.g., sexual/ethnic minority status, lower income or education). Conversely, enablers of vaccination included older age, male gender, White race, active engagement in HIV care, previous vaccination history, recommendations from trusted providers, and higher perceived infection risk or belief in vaccination. The refusal and non-uptake rates for COVID-19 vaccines among PLWH in the USA are considerable and influenced by multiple factors. Interventions should focus on addressing systemic mistrust and psychosocial or structural obstacles while utilizing the existing HIV care framework to increase vaccination rates in this population.

title: Evolution of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease under fitness constraints imposed by folding stability and activity
abstract: Abstract The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) continues to evolve and diversify, leading to the emergence of immune-evasive variants and underscoring the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery. In this context, the main protease (Mpro) represents a potential therapeutic target because of its central role in viral replication and its low similarity to human proteases. However, the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance remain insufficiently explored. Through the analysis of multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, we show that, despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions. Across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants, overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved, although specific variant-substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per-residue interactions and hydrogen-bond patterns. Ensemble dynamics revealed conserved large-scale motions alongside modest substrate-dependent shifts in secondary motions in certain Mpro variants. Overall, SARS-CoV-2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting the suitability of this protein as an effective antiviral target. The findings further suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery due to the ongoing evolution and diversification of SARS-CoV-2, which has led to immune-evasive variants. analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants to investigate the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance.
analysis.methods: Through the analysis of multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, the study examined amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions, assessed substrate recognition, and evaluated ensemble dynamics to understand large-scale motions and secondary motions in certain Mpro variants.
analysis.main_results: Despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in key regions. Overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants, although specific variant-substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per-residue interactions and hydrogen-bond patterns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that SARS-CoV-2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting its suitability as an effective antiviral target. The novelty lies in demonstrating that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the suitability of Mpro as an effective antiviral target and suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help design therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness, which is crucial for combating evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is high, as it directly analyzes multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants and provides detailed insights into their structural and functional constraints. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于正在进行的 进化 和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的多样化导致了免疫逃避变异,该研究解决了针对保守病毒机制的补充 抗病毒药物 策略的需求。它特别关注主要蛋白酶(Mpro)作为潜在的治疗靶点,因为它在病毒复制中发挥核心作用并且与人类蛋白酶的相似性较低。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变异,以研究 Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的进化后果。
elements_zh.methods: 通过对多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体的分析,该研究检查了活性位点和二聚化界面区域中的氨基酸取代,评估了底物识别,并评估了整体动力学,以了解某些 Mpro 变体中的大规模运动和次级运动。
elements_zh.main_results: 尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,关键区域的氨基酸替换有限。尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性,但 Mpro 的总体底物识别在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中很大程度上保留了。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈约束,支持其作为有效的 抗病毒药物 目标的适用性。新颖之处在于证明整合病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持 Mpro 作为有效 抗病毒药物 靶点的适用性,并表明纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有更强长期稳健性的治疗策略,这对于应对不断变化的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度很高,因为它直接分析了多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体,并提供了对其结构和功能限制的详细见解。然而,其局限性包括特定变体-底物对中每个残基相互作用和氢键模式可能存在一些异质性,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。

abstract_zh: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 不断进化和多样化,导致免疫逃避变异体的出现,并强调需要针对保守病毒机制的补充 抗病毒药物 策略。在这种情况下,主要蛋白酶(Mpro)代表了一个潜在的治疗靶点,因为它在病毒复制中发挥着核心作用,并且与人类蛋白酶的相似性较低。然而,Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的进化后果尚未得到充分探索。通过对多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体的分析,我们表明,尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,活性位点和二聚化界面区域的氨基酸替换有限。在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中,Mpro 的整体底物识别在很大程度上得以保留,尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性。整体动力学揭示了某些 Mpro 变体中保守的大规模运动以及次级运动中适度的底物依赖性变化。总体而言,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈限制,支持该蛋白作为有效的 抗病毒药物 靶标的适用性。研究结果进一步表明,纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。

analysis_zh.main_results: 尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,关键区域的氨基酸替换有限。尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性,但 Mpro 的总体底物识别在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中很大程度上保留了。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈约束,支持其作为有效的 抗病毒药物 目标的适用性。新颖之处在于证明整合病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持 Mpro 作为有效 抗病毒药物 靶点的适用性,并表明纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有更强长期稳健性的治疗策略,这对于应对不断变化的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度很高,因为它直接分析了多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体,并提供了对其结构和功能限制的详细见解。然而,其局限性包括特定变体-底物对中每个残基相互作用和氢键模式可能存在一些异质性,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。

title: Understanding neuroinflammation in post-COVID-19 syndrome: biological mechanisms, diagnostic biomarkers, and therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) is an escalating global health concern, marked by persistent cognitive, neurological, and psychiatric symptoms following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Although its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood, mounting evidence implicates chronic neuroinflammation as a key driver. Sustained microglial and astrocyte activation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and aberrant cytokine signaling contribute to prolonged immune dysregulation within the central nervous system, promoting long-term brain dysfunction. In this expert review, we synthesize emerging insights into how neuroimmune processes impair brain function in PCS. We explore novel mechanistic pathways - including local sleep intrusions, impaired memory reconsolidation, and astrocyte-mediated destabilization of functional networks - that may underlie the syndrome's fluctuating and heterogeneous presentation. We evaluate fluid biomarkers of neuroinflammation, including glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), soluble TREM2, S100β, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α. In parallel, we highlight converging neuroimaging biomarkers derived from PET and MRI studies. These include increased TSPO-PET binding in limbic and frontal regions, alterations in cerebral blood flow and oxygen metabolism, neurometabolic changes detected via MR spectroscopy (e.g., elevated myo-inositol and choline), and increased free water content on diffusion imaging - each suggestive of glial activation and network-level dysfunction. We propose a multiscale, longitudinal framework that integrates molecular, neuroimaging, and behavioral data to link immune dysregulation with brain network instability and symptom emergence. Such integrative approaches are critical for advancing precision diagnostics and informing the development of targeted, mechanism-based treatments for individuals affected by PCS.

analysis.summary_en: This expert review examines neuroinflammation in post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS), focusing on biological mechanisms, diagnostic biomarkers, and therapeutic prospects. The review synthesizes evidence on how chronic neuroinflammation, driven by sustained microglial and astrocyte activation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and aberrant cytokine signaling, contributes to prolonged brain dysfunction. It evaluates fluid biomarkers like GFAP, soluble TREM2, and pro-inflammatory cytokines, as well as neuroimaging findings from PET and MRI studies. The authors propose novel mechanistic pathways, including sleep disturbances and memory reconsolidation impairment, and emphasize the need for integrative frameworks to link immune dysregulation with symptom emergence. The review underscores the importance of precision diagnostics and targeted treatments for PCS.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇专家综述,综合了对 PCS 神经炎症的最新见解。该综述评估了神经炎症的液体生物标志物,包括胶质纤维酸性蛋白 (GFAP)、可溶性 TREM2、S100β 和促炎细胞因子,以及来自 PET 和 MRI 研究的神经影像生物标志物。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 持续的小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞激活、血脑屏障破坏和异常的细胞因子信号传导导致中枢神经系统内长期免疫失调,促进长期脑功能障碍。新的机制途径包括局部睡眠入侵、记忆重建受损和星形胶质细胞介导的功能网络不稳定。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: PCS 的基本机制仍不完全清楚。该综述强调需要建立多尺度、纵向框架来将免疫失调与大脑网络不稳定和症状出现联系起来,这表明目前对该综合征的波动性和异质性表现的理解存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 结合分子、神经影像和行为数据的综合方法对于推进精确诊断和为受 PCS 影响的个体开发有针对性的、基于机制的 治疗 至关重要。

title: Understanding parent motivation for participating in the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine trial.
abstract: This study aimed to understand parental motivations and concerns regarding enrollment in the Rutgers SARS-CoV-2 (RSC) pediatric vaccine trial during the COVID-19 pandemic. Among the 64 parents who completed the survey, the most commonly reported motivation for enrollment was altruism and contributing to science (93.8%), followed by the potential benefit to the child (90.6%). All participating parents had received the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine themselves. Despite the novelty of the COVID-19 vaccine and widespread misinformation, parents in this study demonstrated a high level of support for the pediatric vaccine trial. The parents' high education level and personal vaccination status may have influenced these findings. Future research should focus on recruiting a more diverse participant pool to enhance the generalizability of results.

title: Serology and PCR for Apicomplexa and SARS-CoV-2 in feral cats from a Brazilian island.
abstract: Feral cats in insular environments represent a relevant interface between wildlife, environmental contamination, and zoonotic risk under a One Health perspective, as feralization increases exposure to infections and facilitates pathogen transmission. Herein, we surveyed Toxoplasma gondii, Sarcocystis spp., Neospora caninum, and SARS-CoV-2 in Furtada Island, Mangaratiba, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where there has been a feral cat population since the 1950s. This study aimed to investigate serological, molecular, and morphological indicators of infection in feral cats by assessing antibodies against Toxoplasma gondii, Sarcocystis spp., Neospora caninum, and SARS-CoV-2, detecting Apicomplexa DNA in reproductive tissues, and evaluating the morphology of the uterus, ovaries, testes, and epididymides. It was demonstrated that 40.4% (21/52) were exposed to T. gondii, 13.7% (7/52) were exposed to Sarcocystis spp., and no cats were seropositive for N. Additionally, no feline was positive for SARS-CoV-2 through serological investigation. No histological changes were observed in the reproductive tissues, and the DNA of the agents was not detected using molecular methods. This is the first investigation of host-pathogen interaction in feral cats from Furtada Island in southeastern Brazil. The data confirm that Toxoplasma gondii and Sarcocystis spp. are circulating within this feral cat population. These findings highlight the importance of feral cats as sentinels of environmental contamination and support the need for One Health-based surveillance strategies in insular ecosystems.
authors: Leila Maria de Carvalho Alves Dos Santos

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在生殖组织中未检测到组织学变化或病原体 DNA,并且 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 血清阳性的缺失引发了对该野猫群体中 患病率 的疑问。

title: Co-design in action: lessons learned from transplant patient and family engagement in an integrated knowledge translation strategy during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted immunocompromised individuals, particularly transplant recipients. Despite their vulnerability, national- and international-level research often lacks direct input from this community. In response, the Canadian Donation and Transplantation Research Program (CDTRP) implemented an integrated knowledge translation (iKT) strategy that involved patient, family, and donor (PFD) partners as co-leads and decision makers throughout the research process. Beginning in 2022, CDTRP adapted a co-engagement model to identify research priorities and inform study design, conduct, and knowledge mobilization related to COVID-19 issues for transplant recipients. Diverse stakeholders, including researchers, clinicians, policymakers, trainees, transplant-focused organizations, and PFD partners, collectively co-developed the TREAT-COVID research project. In 2022–2023 CDTRP hosted a series of four national forums that were co-designed and co-facilitated by PFD co-leads, enabling shared decision making and iterative refinement of research priorities and strategies. This paper provides an overview of the iKT strategy implemented, including objectives, engagement processes, outputs, resulting study adaptations, and lessons learned. Each forum generated new insights and actionable changes. Forum 1 identified research priorities, including clinical therapeutics, psychosocial needs, quality of life, economic burden, and recovery-related supports. Forum 2 emphasized mental health and support for transplant recipients and their caregivers. Forum 3 identified the distinct but complementary priorities of transplant recipients and their caregivers, such as clinical care and mental wellness, respectively. Forum 4 addressed barriers to recruiting study participants and refined communication strategies. These forums collectively shaped the TREAT-COVID research project by informing study priorities, data collection tools, recruitment strategies, and knowledge mobilization. This paper details the iKT strategy implemented by the CDTRP to engage diverse stakeholders in COVID-19-related research for transplant communities. Meaningful and structured patient and family involvement in national health research during a public health emergency was prioritized. By involving patient and family partners in governance, facilitation, study refinement, recruitment, and dissemination, CDTRP advanced a collaborative and equity-driven iKT model. The paper contributes an operational example of national-scale patient and family co-leadership in time-sensitive research. The COVID-19 pandemic has posed major risks for immunocompromised individuals, including transplant recipients, but their voices are often underrepresented in research. To bridge this gap, the Canadian Donation and Transplantation Research Program (CDTRP) worked with transplant patient and family partners to develop a national research project that included their priorities. Patient and family partners were involved from the beginning, helping to shape research questions, lead meetings, review materials, identify challenges, and decide how results would be shared. In 2022–2023, CDTRP held four national forums to gather information from the transplant community, each with distinct goals. In Forum 1, participants discussed urgent research questions about treatments and mental health challenges faced. In Forum 2, participants refined research priorities, emphasizing mental health and supports for patients and families. In Forum 3, patients and caregivers highlighted distinct needs. In Forum 4, participants explored why transplant recipients and their caregivers and family members might or might not join the study and how to improve participation. title: Broad and durable protection against SARS-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV by an intranasal chimpanzee adenovirus vaccine expressing tandem RBDs and nucleocapsid
abstract: Current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines reduce severe disease but offer limited protection against infection, enabling viral persistence, immune escape, and transmission. We developed intranasal rare-serotype chimpanzee adenovirus 68 (AdC68)–based vaccines expressing heterologous tandem receptor-binding domains from SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV, fused to the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N) to enhance both B and T cell responses. Antigen integrity was confirmed by receptor binding and recognition by multiple conformation-sensitive monoclonal antibodies. In mice, intranasal AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N elicited potent and durable mucosal and systemic immunity, including serum/saliva IgA and broad neutralizing antibodies persisting up to 40 weeks, alongside tissue-localized B and T cells. Monoclonal antibodies from long-lived bone marrow antibody-secreting cells demonstrated broad and strain-specific neutralization, providing mechanistic insight into the breadth and longevity of the antibody response. In Syrian hamsters, intranasal immunization protected against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 replication in nasal turbinates and lungs and blocked transmission for up to four months post-vaccination. Robust protection against SARS-CoV challenge was demonstrated in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice, further confirming its broad efficacy. These findings support AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N as a promising mucosal vaccine candidate to prevent infection and transmission of pathogenic coronaviruses.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 来自长寿骨髓抗体分泌细胞的单克隆抗体表现出广泛的菌株特异性中和作用,为抗体反应的广度和寿命提供了机制上的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在叙利亚仓鼠中,鼻内免疫可防止 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1.5 在鼻甲和肺部复制,并在 疫苗接种 后长达四个月内阻断 传播。

title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (BEEHIVE trial).
abstract: BACKGROUND Real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) and relative VE (rVE) data of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections inform policy recommendations and reinforce public confidence. The study aim was to assess the safety and VE of the 2023-2024 protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5) in a real-world setting. METHODS The single-site, pragmatic BEEHIVE clinical trial was conducted among participants aged ≥18 years from the Salt Lake City, Utah, area, who had previously received ≥2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, from November 17, 2023, through September 9, 2024. Randomized participants received a protein-based or mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in a double-blind manner. An unblinded, nonrandomized comparator control group that did not receive a study vaccine was also enrolled. The primary aim measured VE between the randomized and comparator groups. The secondary aim was to measure rVE between the 2 vaccine platforms. In the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis, VE and rVE were estimated using a proportional-hazards model for symptomatic infections confirmed by weekly self-administered rapid antigen tests (RATs) over 24 weeks, adjusted for covariates. Reactogenicity and treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were recorded. RESULTS Randomized cohorts (N = 909; protein-based, n = 452; mRNA, n = 457) were largely well-balanced with some differences in baseline covariates versus the comparator group (n = 279), mostly age-related. The mITT population had 142 RAT-confirmed symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 cases with an adjusted VE of 43.6% (95% CI, 18.3-61.0); rVE (protein-based vs mRNA) was -26.7% (90% CI, -78.6% to 10.1%) and did not reach statistical significance. Safety and reactogenicity were comparable to previously reported findings, with no serious study vaccine-related TEAEs, myocarditis/pericarditis, hospitalization, or death. CONCLUSIONS This is one of the earliest real-world trials evaluating the VE of the 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5). These results suggest that both protein-based and mRNA vaccines are well-tolerated and significantly reduce the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on individuals working in otolaryngology: a cross-sectional survey.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The COVID-19 pandemic is caused by the highly infectious and transmissible SARS-CoV-2 virus. Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (OHNS) practice is at high risk of transmission and subsequently affected by guideline changes and procedure cancellations or postponements. We aimed to gather opinions regarding the pandemic's personal and professional impact from OHNS professionals globally. STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: A cross-sectional survey was developed and administered using snowball sampling for surgical staff, trainees, and connected allied health workers in OHNS globally in May 2021. METHODS: Item generation was developed via selection of measures from an existing global perspectives survey with additional measures piloted by clinical context experts, service providers, and researchers. RESULTS: The majority of the 452 total responses were collected from the Americas (68.9%) and identified as female (64.4%). The most commonly reported workplace challenge was fear of illness (21.1%). Respondents generally favoured policies implemented by local health authorities (69.7%) but believed that policies were implemented too late (49.6%). Three main themes surfaced: 1) Unclear guidelines for allied OHNS professionals, 2) Fear regarding COVID-19 transmission due to varied understanding of transmission and PPE adoption, and 3) Resilience of OHNS workers despite continued professional and personal challenges. CONCLUSION: Individuals reported generalized fear and frustration in their personal and professional lives due to COVID-19 pandemic. However, they exhibited agility to overcome these challenges. Ongoing support from government and OHNS societies is key to aid health professionals providing essential care. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, cohort cross-sectional survey.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focused on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, caused by SARS-CoV-2, on professionals in otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (OHNS) globally, examining personal and professional challenges faced by surgical staff, trainees, and allied health workers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional survey using snowball sampling was administered in May 2021 to OHNS professionals worldwide. Item generation involved selecting measures from an existing global perspectives survey and piloting additional measures with clinical experts, service providers, and researchers.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: OHNS professionals reported generalized fear and frustration in personal and professional lives due to the pandemic, but demonstrated agility to overcome challenges. Key themes included unclear guidelines for allied professionals, fear of transmission due to varied understanding of transmission and PPE adoption, and resilience despite ongoing challenges.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study identified unclear guidelines for allied OHNS professionals and inconsistent understanding of COVID-19 transmission and PPE adoption as major issues. Additionally, there was a perception that policies were implemented too late by health authorities.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Ongoing support from government and OHNS societies is crucial to aid health professionals providing essential care. Addressing unclear guidelines and improving communication about transmission risks and PPE protocols are key priorities.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional survey examined the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on otolaryngology professionals globally, conducted in May 2021 with 452 respondents. The study found that OHNS workers faced significant challenges, including fear of illness (21.1%) and frustration with delayed policy implementation (49.6%). Key themes emerged: unclear guidelines for allied professionals, inconsistent understanding of transmission and PPE use, and remarkable resilience despite ongoing difficulties. While participants reported generalized fear and frustration, they demonstrated agility in overcoming these challenges. The study emphasizes the need for ongoing support from governments and OHNS societies to maintain essential care delivery and addresses gaps in guideline clarity and communication about transmission risks.

title_zh: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on individuals working in otolaryngology: a cross-sectional survey.
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The COVID-19 pandemic is caused by the highly infectious and transmissible SARS-CoV-2 virus. Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (OHNS) practice is at high risk of transmission and subsequently affected by guideline changes and procedure cancellations or postponements. We aimed to gather opinions regarding the pandemic's personal and professional impact from OHNS professionals globally. STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: A cross-sectional survey was developed and administered using snowball sampling for surgical staff, trainees, and connected allied health workers in OHNS globally in May 2021. METHODS: Item generation was developed via selection of measures from an existing global perspectives survey with additional measures piloted by clinical context experts, service providers, and researchers. RESULTS: The majority of the 452 total responses were collected from the Americas (68.9%) and identified as female (64.4%). The most commonly reported workplace challenge was fear of illness (21.1%). Respondents generally favoured policies implemented by local health authorities (69.7%) but believed that policies were implemented too late (49.6%). Three main themes surfaced: 1) Unclear guidelines for allied OHNS professionals, 2) Fear regarding COVID-19 transmission due to varied understanding of transmission and PPE adoption, and 3) Resilience of OHNS workers despite continued professional and personal challenges. CONCLUSION: Individuals reported generalized fear and frustration in their personal and professional lives due to COVID-19 pandemic. However, they exhibited agility to overcome these challenges. Ongoing support from government and OHNS societies is key to aid health professionals providing essential care. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, cohort cross-sectional survey.

title: Abnormal uterine bleeding during the COVID-19 pandemic among reproductive-age women with and without HIV.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Women have reported abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Evaluating AUB among women living with HIV (WWH) and women without HIV (WWoH) during the COVID-19 pandemic is key to understanding reproductive health in the setting of viral co-infections. METHODS: From 2021 to 2023, the Study of Treatment and Reproductive Outcomes (STAR) collected cross-sectional data from WWH and WWoH 18-45 years-of-age across the southern United States without conditions known to interfere with menses. Women completed surveys on COVID-19 testing, COVID-19 vaccination, AUB (spotting, missed periods, early/late periods), stress, and demographics. We tested plasma from participants at two study sites for COVID-19 antibodies. We defined "prior SARS-CoV-2 infection" as having detectable anti-nucleocapsid antibodies or a self-reported positive COVID-19 test. We examined AUB in association with COVID-19 vaccination and infection stratified by HIV status. RESULTS: Among 188 eligible women, 61% were living with HIV, 49% had AUB, and 58% were vaccinated for COVID-19. When assessed via combined self-report and antibody tests (n = 86), 69% of women had prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. There were no differences in AUB, COVID-19 vaccination, or SARS-CoV-2 infection by HIV status. Among the entire sample of WWoH (n = 73), AUB was associated with lower age (32 vs. 35, p = 0.04) and higher perceived stress (17 vs. 13, p = 0.04), and AUB was more common in WWoH who self-reported a positive COVID-19 test versus WWoH without (70% vs. AUB was not associated with COVID-19 vaccination, body mass index, race, or ethnicity. In WWoH with antibody testing (n = 42), AUB remained more common among WWoH with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection versus WWoH without (61% vs. Among WWH, no variables were associated with AUB. CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating, descriptive study, AUB was associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, stress, and age among WWoH, but not among WWH. There was no association between AUB and COVID-19 vaccination.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) among reproductive-age women with and without HIV during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on associations with COVID-19 vaccination and infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional study conducted from 2021 to 2023 as part of the Study of Treatment and Reproductive Outcomes (STAR), collecting data from women aged 18-45 across the southern United States without conditions interfering with menses. Plasma was tested for COVID-19 antibodies at two study sites.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: AUB was associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, stress, and lower age among women without HIV, but not among women with HIV. No association was found between AUB and COVID-19 vaccination, body mass index, race, or ethnicity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study is hypothesis-generating and descriptive, with limitations including potential selection bias and the small sample size. No variables were associated with AUB among women with HIV, suggesting possible differences in pathophysiology or immune response that warrant further investigation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore the mechanisms linking SARS-CoV-2 infection to AUB in women without HIV and investigate why no association was observed in women with HIV. Clinicians should consider stress and COVID-19 infection as potential factors in AUB among reproductive-age women.

Among women without HIV, AUB was associated with younger age, higher stress, and prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. No association was found with vaccination or other factors. Among women with HIV, no variables were associated with AUB. The study suggests potential differences in how SARS-CoV-2 infection affects AUB based on HIV status.

title: Post COVID-19 condition diagnosis among older people: findings from Swedish national register data.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Post COVID-19 condition (PCC) denotes the persistence of symptoms following Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. PCC poses a large disease burden worldwide. We aimed to explore the epidemiological characteristics of clinically diagnosed PCC among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden and to establish a machine learning tool to predict PCC risk. METHODS: This nationwide register-based study employed a cross-sectional design. Prevalence of PCC diagnosis recorded in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden was calculated. Logistic regression models were employed to assess the associations between various factors and PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care. A prediction model based on extreme gradient boosting was constructed based on selected features. RESULTS: Of 236,943 older people aged ≥65 years who were diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% of them were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care. The odds of PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care in women were lower (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82). The odds decreased for each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98). Higher odds of PCC were found in people with higher Charlson Comorbidity Index and who used more types of medication. analysis.research_question_and_background: Post COVID-19 condition (PCC) denotes the persistence of symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection and poses a large disease burden worldwide.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This nationwide register-based study employed a cross-sectional design to explore the epidemiological characteristics of clinically diagnosed PCC among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden.
analysis.methods: The prevalence of PCC diagnosis was calculated in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings, and logistic regression models were employed to assess associations between various factors and PCC, along with constructing a prediction model based on extreme gradient boosting.
analysis.main_results: Of 236,943 older people diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care; women had lower odds (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82), and odds decreased with each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The prevalence of PCC diagnosis among older people in Sweden was relatively low when restricted to hospital and specialized outpatient care, and register-based predictive models may help identify older people at higher risk of PCC.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings can inform targeted surveillance and early intervention strategies for older adults at higher risk of PCC, particularly those with higher comorbidity burden and more medication use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on register-based data, which may underrepresent PCC cases not diagnosed in hospital or specialized outpatient care.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide register-based study investigated the epidemiological characteristics of post COVID-19 condition (PCC) among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden. Using a cross-sectional design, the researchers calculated the prevalence of clinically diagnosed PCC in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings and developed a machine learning prediction tool. Among 236,943 COVID-19 cases, 2.5% were diagnosed with PCC, with lower odds in women and decreasing odds with age. Higher comorbidity burden and more medication use were associated with increased PCC odds, while infections during the Omicron-predominant period had the lowest odds. The study provides moderate evidence that register-based models can help identify high-risk older adults for targeted interventions.

We aimed to explore the epidemiological characteristics of clinically diagnosed PCC among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden and to establish a machine learning tool to predict PCC risk. METHODS: This nationwide register-based study employed a cross-sectional design. Prevalence of PCC diagnosis recorded in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden was calculated. Logistic regression models were employed to assess the associations between various factors and PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care. A prediction model based on extreme gradient boosting was constructed based on selected features. RESULTS: Of 236,943 older people aged ≥65 years who were diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% of them were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care. The odds of PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care in women were lower (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82). The odds decreased for each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98). Higher odds of PCC were found in people with higher Charlson Comorbidity Index and who used more types of medication. The odds of PCC were the lowest for infections during Omicron-predominant period (OR = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.08-0.10). The predicted PCC risk was generally higher among individuals aged 65-74 years with higher comorbidity burden, more types of medication use, and during early variant-dominant periods. CONCLUSION: In summary, the prevalence of PCC diagnosis among older people in Sweden was relatively low when restricted to hospital and specialized outpatient care. A higher burden of comorbidities and more types of medication use were associated with increased odds of PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care. Register-based predictive models may help identify older people at higher risk of PCC.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项全国性的登记研究采用横断面设计来探讨瑞典 65 岁以上老年人中临床诊断的 PCC 的流行病学特征。
analysis_zh.methods: PCC 诊断 的 患病率 在医院和专科门诊护理环境中计算,并采用逻辑回归模型评估各种因素与 PCC 之间的关联,并构建基于极端梯度提升的预测模型。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 当仅限于医院和专门门诊护理时,瑞典老年人中 PCC 诊断 的 患病率 相对较低,基于登记的预测模型可能有助于识别 PCC 风险较高的老年人。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为 PCC 风险较高的老年人,特别是那些合并症负担较高和药物使用较多的老年人提供有针对性的 监测 和早期干预策略。

title: Challenges and Opportunities for Signal Detection During Public Health Emergencies: An Historical Re-evaluation of the Disproportionality Analysis of the ADR Reporting of Anti-COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibodies in Vigibase.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Anti-spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for early treatment of COVID-19 represented a significant improvement in the pharmacological management of the SARS-COV-2 pandemic, especially in early phases, but the continuous emergence of novel virus variants of concern (VoC) required a rapid and continuous benefit-risk assessment. OBJECTIVE: To identify possible unexplored safety signals of anti-SARS-CoV-2 mAbs through disproportionality analysis using VigiBase, the World Health Organization (WHO) global pharmacovigilance database. METHODS: We conducted a disproportionality analysis of VigiBase (February 2020-December 2023). All de-duplicated individual case safety reports (ICSRs) for bamlanivimab, bamlanivimab/etesevimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, regdanvimab, sotrovimab, and tixagevimab/cilgavimab were retrieved. Descriptive analyses of ICSRs and distribution of suspected adverse drug reactions across VoC-defined periods (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) were performed. Disproportionality analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the READUS-PV guideline. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated at the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) level, using the entire database as reference (excluding vaccines). Statistically significant drug-adverse reaction pairs included in the EMA Important Medical Event (IME) list and not described in the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) were identified as potential safety signals. RESULTS: Among 15,250 de-duplicated ICSRs, casirivimab/imdevimab accounted for the majority of reports (33.5%). Most cases involved female patients aged 45-64 years, predominantly reported from the Americas. Overall, 42,799 drug-adverse reaction pairs were identified, 33,948 (79.3%) of which were identified after filtering out, and 3047 (9.0%) were IMEs. Eighty-three unique drug-adverse reaction pairs had a statistically significant RORs, among which 56 (67.5%) were not listed in the SmPC. Bamlanivimab, as both monotherapy and in combination with etesevimab, showed increased reporting of several cardiac adverse events, including acute myocardial infarction (MI) and cardiac arrest. For tixagevimab/cilgavimab, disproportionality was found for acute MI (N = 6; ROR 12.7, 95% CI 5.7-28.4) and atrial fibrillation (N = 29; ROR 9.0, 95% CI 6.2-13.0). For regdanvimab, disproportionality emerged for hypokalemia (N = 13; ROR 5.8, 95% CI 3.4-10.1). For casirivimab/imdevimab, 5 out of 15 PTs were classified as adverse event of special interest: seizure-like phenomena (N = 8; ROR, 44.2; 95% CI 21.9-89.1), Guillain-Barré syndrome (N = 6; ROR 13.4, 95% CI 6.0-30.0), encephalopathy (N = 13; ROR 5.4, 95% CI 3.1-9.3), generalized tonic-clonic seizure (N = 9; ROR 5.0, 95% CI 2.6-9.7), and seizure (N = 57; ROR 3.1, 95% CI 2.4-4.0). CONCLUSION: This analysis identified potential cardiovascular and neurological safety signals, which will remain unexplored by longitudinal pharmacoepidemiologic studies due to the withdrawal of these agents from clinical use. Overall, this case study supported the full implementation of near real-time multimodal approaches to efficiently perform actionable signal management during public health emergencies.

title_zh: Challenges and Opportunities for Signal Detection During Public Health Emergencies: An Historical Re-evaluation of the Disproportionality Analysis of the ADR Reporting of Anti-COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibodies in Vigibase.
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Anti-spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for early treatment of COVID-19 represented a significant improvement in the pharmacological management of the SARS-COV-2 pandemic, especially in early phases, but the continuous emergence of novel virus variants of concern (VoC) required a rapid and continuous benefit-risk assessment. OBJECTIVE: To identify possible unexplored safety signals of anti-SARS-CoV-2 mAbs through disproportionality analysis using VigiBase, the World Health Organization (WHO) global pharmacovigilance database. METHODS: We conducted a disproportionality analysis of VigiBase (February 2020-December 2023). All de-duplicated individual case safety reports (ICSRs) for bamlanivimab, bamlanivimab/etesevimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, regdanvimab, sotrovimab, and tixagevimab/cilgavimab were retrieved. Descriptive analyses of ICSRs and distribution of suspected adverse drug reactions across VoC-defined periods (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) were performed. Disproportionality analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the READUS-PV guideline. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated at the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) level, using the entire database as reference (excluding vaccines). Statistically significant drug-adverse reaction pairs included in the EMA Important Medical Event (IME) list and not described in the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) were identified as potential safety signals. RESULTS: Among 15,250 de-duplicated ICSRs, casirivimab/imdevimab accounted for the majority of reports (33.5%). Most cases involved female patients aged 45-64 years, predominantly reported from the Americas. Overall, 42,799 drug-adverse reaction pairs were identified, 33,948 (79.3%) of which were identified after filtering out, and 3047 (9.0%) were IMEs. Eighty-three unique drug-adverse reaction pairs had a statistically significant RORs, among which 56 (67.5%) were not listed in the SmPC. Bamlanivimab, as both monotherapy and in combination with etesevimab, showed increased reporting of several cardiac adverse events, including acute myocardial infarction (MI) and cardiac arrest. For tixagevimab/cilgavimab, disproportionality was found for acute MI (N = 6; ROR 12.7, 95% CI 5.7-28.4) and atrial fibrillation (N = 29; ROR 9.0, 95% CI 6.2-13.0). For regdanvimab, disproportionality emerged for hypokalemia (N = 13; ROR 5.8, 95% CI 3.4-10.1). For casirivimab/imdevimab, 5 out of 15 PTs were classified as adverse event of special interest: seizure-like phenomena (N = 8; ROR, 44.2; 95% CI 21.9-89.1), Guillain-Barré syndrome (N = 6; ROR 13.4, 95% CI 6.0-30.0), encephalopathy (N = 13; ROR 5.4, 95% CI 3.1-9.3), generalized tonic-clonic seizure (N = 9; ROR 5.0, 95% CI 2.6-9.7), and seizure (N = 57; ROR 3.1, 95% CI 2.4-4.0). CONCLUSION: This analysis identified potential cardiovascular and neurological safety signals, which will remain unexplored by longitudinal pharmacoepidemiologic studies due to the withdrawal of these agents from clinical use. Overall, this case study supported the full implementation of near real-time multimodal approaches to efficiently perform actionable signal management during public health emergencies.

title: Deep mutational scanning of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid reveals regional stability patterns.
abstract: Point mutations within the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) have the potential to impact not only detection but the viral life cycle, and therefore pathogenicity. Leveraging deep mutational scanning (DMS) we determine the effect of 7876 (98.9%) of all possible point mutations on NP surface expression as a proxy for stability, which we term surface-expression-based folding fitness (SEBFF). We show NP susceptibility to SEBFF changes varies with region, with mutations to the structured RNA-binding domain (RBD) and dimerization domain (DD) being more likely to cause decreases in SEBFF. We show that the R203K mutation in the linker region increases the folding fitness of NP, suggesting thermostability may have been one factor driving the adoption of the R203K/G204R set of mutations arising in the alpha, gamma and omicron lineages. Our DMS results appear consistent with the limited recombinant protein and biophysical data for NP variants available from the literature. We tested three computational methods to determine whether any could accurately predict the DMS data; per-variant predictions were poor, but per-site predictions were good, with machine learning methods outperforming the physics-based strategy, and ThermoMPNN-D performing most effectively with the RBD and ProteinMPNN with the DD.

The findings align with limited existing biophysical data and provide insights into viral evolution and mutation impacts.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳的深度突变扫描揭示了区域稳定性模式。
source_body_en: Point mutations within the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) have the potential to impact not only detection but the viral life cycle, and therefore pathogenicity. Leveraging deep mutational scanning (DMS) we determine the effect of 7876 (98.9%) of all possible point mutations on NP surface expression as a proxy for stability, which we term surface-expression-based folding fitness (SEBFF). We show NP susceptibility to SEBFF changes varies with region, with mutations to the structured RNA-binding domain (RBD) and dimerization domain (DD) being more likely to cause decreases in SEBFF. We show that the R203K mutation in the linker region increases the folding fitness of NP, suggesting thermostability may have been one factor driving the adoption of the R203K/G204R set of mutations arising in the alpha, gamma and omicron lineages. Our DMS results appear consistent with the limited recombinant protein and biophysical data for NP variants available from the literature. We tested three computational methods to determine whether any could accurately predict the DMS data; per-variant predictions were poor, but per-site predictions were good, with machine learning methods outperforming the physics-based strategy, and ThermoMPNN-D performing most effectively with the RBD and ProteinMPNN with the DD.

title: Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Variant-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can induce more robust immune responses against closely matched circulating variants than original vaccines. METHODS: Within a phase 3 master study, monovalent Omicron BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 (BNT162b2-BA.1) was evaluated in healthy BNT162b2-experienced (cohorts 1-2) or COVID-19 vaccine-naive (cohort 3) 18 to 55 year-olds. Primary immunogenicity endpoints in cohort 1 were geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Omicron BA.1 neutralizing titers 1 month after BNT162b2-BA.1 to those after one BNT162b2 dose and differences in percentages of participants with Omicron BA.1 seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2. In cohort 2, primary immunogenicity objectives (participants without evidence of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection) were to demonstrate superiority (GMR two-sided 95% CI lower limit > 1) with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse difference (difference two-sided 95% CI lower limit > - 5%) for BNT162b2-BA.1 versus BNT162b2. In cohort 3, primary immunogenicity objectives were to demonstrate superiority with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse after two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses compared with participants receiving BNT162b2 in an efficacy trial. Reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were determined. RESULTS: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1 (BNT162b2-experienced), GMRs compared with one BNT162b2 dose were 2.87 and 2.64 after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively, and differences in percentages of participants with seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 were 29.0% and 21.0% for one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses. In cohort 2 (BNT162b2-experienced), one BNT162b2-BA.1 dose met prespecified superiority and noninferiority criteria with respect to GMR and difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse, respectively, compared with BNT162b2. In cohort 3 (COVID-19 vaccine-naive), superiority with respect to GMR and noninferiority with respect to difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse of BNT162b2-BA.1 to BNT162b2 were met. BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 safety and tolerability profiles were similar. CONCLUSIONS: Omicron BA.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can broaden immune responses against Omicron BA.1 SARS-CoV-2 variants. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT04955626.

title_original: Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in individuals previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive, addressing the need for updated vaccines against circulating variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 3 master study was conducted in healthy 18- to 55-year-olds, divided into three cohorts: those previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 (cohorts 1-2) and those who were vaccine-naive (cohort 3).
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed through geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of neutralizing titers and seroresponse percentages, while reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were monitored.
analysis.main_results: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1, GMRs after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses were 2.87 and 2.64, respectively, compared with one BNT162b2 dose. Seroresponse differences were 29.0% and 21.0% for one and two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrated that BNT162b2-BA.1 induced higher neutralizing titers and greater seroresponse rates compared to the original vaccine, indicating its potential to improve immune responses against the Omicron BA.1 variant.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may enhance protection against emerging variants, supporting their use in booster campaigns and informing future vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to individuals aged 18-55 years, and the evidence is based on immunogenicity measures rather than clinical outcomes, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in 18- to 55-year-olds previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive. The phase 3 master study compared the vaccine's performance against the original BNT162b2 vaccine, showing higher neutralizing titers and seroresponse rates in vaccinated individuals. In vaccine-naive participants, the BA.1-adapted vaccine also met superiority and noninferiority criteria. Safety profiles were similar between the vaccines. The results suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may improve immune responses against the Omicron variant, supporting their use in booster campaigns. However, the study's focus on immunogenicity rather than clinical outcomes limits its generalizability.
